root_cause: The PyTorch Layer Tests pytest process on the Windows runner crashed with a native 'Windows fatal exception: access violation' (equivalent of SIGSEGV) while executing TestFill::test_fill, immediately after the preceding parametrized case PASSED. The crash occurs deep inside the native PyTorch/OpenVINO interop stack reached via pytorch_layer_test_class.py:289 (_test) -> test_full.py:144 (test_fill), with no Python-level exception or assertion - consistent with memory corruption or an unguarded native pointer/buffer access during inference comparison rather than a deterministic logic bug in the PR under test. The PR (#39107) only changes a GPU OpenCL convolution kernel and its CPU-side test file; it does not touch the Windows PyTorch frontend/test harness, so the crash is unrelated to the PR's changes. This matches five prior 'Flaky Test' investigations in the repo-memory database describing intermittent Windows STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION crashes (0xC0000005) in unrelated test processes (benchmark_app, CoreThreadingTests, PyTorch FFT tests, EasyOCR NPU tests) on this same CI fleet, pointing to a known, pre-existing Windows-runner-level flakiness rather than a new regression.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally - this is an intermittent native crash tied to the Windows CI runner environment. To attempt reproduction: on a Windows machine, build OpenVINO with the Release/VS2022 configuration, then run `pytest install/tests/layer_tests/pytorch_tests/test_full.py -k TestFill` repeatedly (the crash is intermittent and may require many iterations to reproduce).
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'PyTorch Layer Tests' job; this failure category is a known transient Windows access-violation flake unrelated to PR #39107's GPU kernel change.

If the crash recurs consistently for TestFill::test_fill specifically (not just intermittently), file a tracking issue to investigate native memory safety in the PyTorch-to-OpenVINO conversion path exercised by TestFill on Windows.
Consider adding a Windows-specific retry/quarantine marker for test_full.py::TestFill if this signature keeps recurring across unrelated PRs.
prevention_strategies: Track recurrence of 'Windows fatal exception: access violation' crashes across all PyTorch/C++ layer test jobs in the pattern database (as already done here); if the same signature or job recurs 3+ times within 12 hours, escalate per the merge-queue recurring-failure policy. Consider enabling Windows crash dump collection (e.g., via Watson/WER or faulthandler core dumps) uploaded as artifacts so future investigations can inspect the actual faulting address instead of only a bare stack frame with no native symbol information.
historical_context: At least 5 prior investigations recorded similar Windows STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION / fatal exception crashes in otherwise-unrelated PRs: benchmark_app crashes (2026-07-07, 2026-07-13 x2), CoreThreadingTests.ReadModel crash (2026-07-08), PyTorch FFT Layer Tests crash in torch.randn (2026-07-14), and EasyOCR NPU Model Hub crash (2026-09-17) - all categorized 'Flaky Test' and judged unrelated to their respective PR diffs. This is the first occurrence of this exact signature (TestFill::test_fill), so a new pattern record is created rather than incrementing an existing one, though it is one instance of a broader recurring class of Windows access-violation flakiness.
